messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: loop in a matrix
parts:
Hi Bic,

You can do this with the sapply() or vapply() functions, which will perform a function you specify on each element in your matrix. My approach was to use the y matrix create another matrix of TRUE’s and FALSE’s corresponding to the bad and good elements of x. Then I set all of the elements of x that are in the same position as the TRUE’s to NA.

Let me know if this doesn’t get you what you want!

Mike


x<-matrix(c(1,5,6,3,2,1), nrow=2, ncol=3)
y<-matrix(c(132,15,36,103,2000,154), nrow=2, ncol=3)  

# This function will take an integer, decompose it into a 32 element vector of "raw" values, take the 3rd element (corresponding to the 4's place) and then converts that value to TRUE or FALSE.
badCellCheck <- function(x) {
  as.logical(intToBits(x)[3])
}

# We can use sapply or vapply to perform a function to every element in an object (a matrix in this case). We apply our badCellCheck() function to each element of y, and then use the structure() function to specify that we want the result to have the same dimensions as y.
badCellIdx <- structure(sapply(y, FUN= badCellCheck), dim= dim(y))

# Here is an alternative way to do the same thing as above. vapply() will be a bit faster because we also specify that the result of the function is a logical (a TRUE or a FALSE). Since R doesn't have to figure this out on its own, this will perform faster which could matter if your matrix is really large.
badCellIdx <- structure(vapply(y, FUN= badCellCheck, FUN.VALUE= logical(1)), dim= dim(y))

# Here is the result of that operation:
badCellIdx

# Now we can use the matrix of TRUE's and FALSE's as an indexing matrix. All of the elements in the x matrix that correspond to the TRUE elements in the badCellIdx matrix will be assigned NA.
x[badCellIdx] <- NA
x

messages.subject: Re: loop in a matrix
parts:
You can concatenate your index, and then use the any() function, which returns TRUE if there are any TRUEs in a vector.

To make the function more general:

badCellCheck <- function(x, idx = c(3,6,9)) # Default values are 3,6,9 - but give the option to over-ride with different index positions
 {
   as.logical(any(intToBits(x)[idx]))
}

Matt
